item.title: GitLab CI and Harbor Registry Integration Pipeline Implementation for Air-Gapped Clusters
item.description:
In air-gapped environments where internet connectivity is restricted or completely disconnected, outbound communication to external public registries (such as Docker Hub or Quay.io) is blocked by firewalls. When operating a Kubernetes cluster using Kubespray in such infrastructure, if container image dependency resolution includes public endpoints, the build pipeline will halt due to timeouts or name resolution errors. To ensure reproducibility in the container build process and eliminate unintended external network requests, a static validation gate with an internal private registry as a prerequisite and a pipeline configuration dedicated to isolated environments are essential.

This article outlines the implementation specifications of a GitLab CI/CD pipeline designed to securely generate, validate, and distribute workload images deployed to a Kubespray cluster, built upon the internal registry “Harbor”.

Overall Pipeline Architecture and Execution Base Parameters

In the target environment, the GitLab Runner itself is placed within the isolated network, constraining target nodes via the docker and offline execution tags. The global configuration used across the entire pipeline is as follows:

stages:
 - validate
 - build

variables:
 HARBOR_REGISTRY: "harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443"
 HARBOR_PROJECT: "kubespray"
 IMAGE_NAME: "nginx-app"

image: "$HARBOR_REGISTRY/$HARBOR_PROJECT/ci/docker:29.1.4-cli"

Configuration Parameter Specifications

  1. stages definition: Composed of validate (a static validation phase to inspect whether the Dockerfile in the repository correctly references the base image from the internal registry) and build (a phase that performs authentication against the internal Harbor, image tag generation based on commit metadata, container image build and push, and environment variable metadata output).

  2. variables definition: Specifies the private Harbor’s FQDN and TLS communication port (harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443) in HARBOR_REGISTRY, and sets the project namespace (kubespray) to isolate and store Kubespray artifacts in HARBOR_PROJECT. Additionally, defines the target workload container image name (nginx-app) in IMAGE_NAME.

  3. Execution image (image): The runner container itself does not rely on a public registry and is pulled from harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/ci/docker:29.1.4-cli. Pinning the version to 29.1.4-cli prevents build failures caused by behavioral discrepancies in CLI options.

Detailed Job Design by Stage

1. Dockerfile Static Validation Job (validate:dockerfile)

Before entering the build process, validate whether unauthorized FROM clauses referencing external registries have been introduced.

validate:dockerfile:
 stage: validate
 tags:
 - docker
 - offline
 script:
 - test -f Dockerfile
 - grep -q "$HARBOR_REGISTRY" Dockerfile
 - echo "Dockerfile validation passed"

💡 test -f Dockerfile verifies the existence of the Dockerfile in the root directory, and grep -q “$HARBOR_REGISTRY” Dockerfile inspects whether the base image reference line contains harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443. If a statement directly specifying an external repository (e.g., FROM nginx:latest) exists, the exit status becomes non-zero, immediately blocking subsequent build job execution.

2. Build and Registry Distribution Job (build:push)

Handles container builds, secure credentials delivery, physical suppression of external requests, and pipeline integration of dynamic metadata.

build:push:
 stage: build
 tags:
 - docker
 - offline
 before_script:
 - docker version
 - echo "$HARBOR_PASSWORD" | docker login "$HARBOR_REGISTRY" -u "$HARBOR_USER" --password-stdin
 script:
 - |
 if [ -n "$CI_COMMIT_TAG" ]; then
 IMAGE_TAG="$CI_COMMIT_TAG"
 else
 IMAGE_TAG="sha-$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA"
 fi

 IMAGE_URI="$HARBOR_REGISTRY/$HARBOR_PROJECT/$IMAGE_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG"

 echo "IMAGE_TAG=$IMAGE_TAG"
 echo "IMAGE_URI=$IMAGE_URI"

 docker build --pull=false -t "$IMAGE_URI" .
 docker push "$IMAGE_URI"

 echo "IMAGE_TAG=$IMAGE_TAG" > build.env
 echo "IMAGE_URI=$IMAGE_URI" >> build.env
 artifacts:
 reports:
 dotenv: build.env
 expire_in: 7 days
 rules:
 - if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "master"'
 - if: '$CI_COMMIT_TAG'

Technical Implementation Highlights

🛠️ Credential Obfuscation: Uses echo “$HARBOR_PASSWORD” | docker login … –password-stdin to prevent password exposure via command-line arguments (plaintext output to process trees or Runner logs).

⚙️ Dynamic Tag Logic: When a release tag is created ($CI_COMMIT_TAG), that tag name is used directly. For branch commits, a unique immutable tag in the format sha-<short-hash> is assigned.

⚠️ External Communication Suppression Flag (–pull=false): Standard docker build may query the remote repository for the latest layer even if a local cache exists. Explicitly specifying –pull=false completely blocks delays and timeout errors caused by unnecessary external probe requests in an isolated environment.

📦 Variable Propagation to Downstream Pipelines: Outputs IMAGE_TAG and IMAGE_URI to the build.env file, passing them to subsequent deployment pipelines (such as Kubespray Playbook execution jobs) via GitLab’s artifacts:reports:dotenv feature.

Integrated Configuration File (.gitlab-ci.yml)

The complete pipeline configuration integrating all jobs is as follows:

stages:
 - validate
 - build

variables:
 HARBOR_REGISTRY: "harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443"
 HARBOR_PROJECT: "kubespray"
 IMAGE_NAME: "nginx-app"

image: "$HARBOR_REGISTRY/$HARBOR_PROJECT/ci/docker:29.1.4-cli"

validate:dockerfile:
 stage: validate
 tags:
 - docker
 - offline
 script:
 - test -f Dockerfile
 - grep -q "$HARBOR_REGISTRY" Dockerfile
 - echo "Dockerfile validation passed"

build:push:
 stage: build
 tags:
 - docker
 - offline
 before_script:
 - docker version
 - echo "$HARBOR_PASSWORD" | docker login "$HARBOR_REGISTRY" -u "$HARBOR_USER" --password-stdin
 script:
 - |
 if [ -n "$CI_COMMIT_TAG" ]; then
 IMAGE_TAG="$CI_COMMIT_TAG"
 else
 IMAGE_TAG="sha-$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA"
 fi

 IMAGE_URI="$HARBOR_REGISTRY/$HARBOR_PROJECT/$IMAGE_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG"

 echo "IMAGE_TAG=$IMAGE_TAG"
 echo "IMAGE_URI=$IMAGE_URI"

 docker build --pull=false -t "$IMAGE_URI" .
 docker push "$IMAGE_URI"

 echo "IMAGE_TAG=$IMAGE_TAG" > build.env
 echo "IMAGE_URI=$IMAGE_URI" >> build.env
 artifacts:
 reports:
 dotenv: build.env
 expire_in: 7 days
 rules:
 - if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "master"'
 - if: '$CI_COMMIT_TAG'

Troubleshooting

Documents common failure modes and resolution steps encountered during CI execution in isolated network environments.

1. TLS/x509 Certificate Verification Error on Non-Standard Port (8443)

Failure Symptom: If Harbor uses port 8443 and is secured by a self-signed certificate from an internal private certificate authority (CA), executing docker login fails with the following error and halts the job:

Error response from daemon: Get "https://harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/v2/": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

Resolution Steps: Place the internal root CA certificate on the Docker daemon of the Runner host. Docker automatically references the path /etc/docker/certs.d/<registry-hostname:port>/ca.crt.

sudo mkdir -p /etc/docker/certs.d/harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443
sudo cp /path/to/internal-ca.crt /etc/docker/certs.d/harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/ca.crt
sudo systemctl restart docker

2. Missing Base Layer Error When --pull=false Is Specified

Failure Symptom: If –pull=false is specified while the base image referenced in the Dockerfile does not exist in the local cache of the Runner host, the build fails as follows:

ERROR: failed to solve: harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/base-nginx:1.25: not found: image not present locally and --pull=false set

Resolution Steps: Add a step in before_script to pre-fetch the necessary base image from Harbor into the local pool before job execution, or explicitly preload the image prior to the initial build.

docker pull harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/base-nginx:1.25

Execution Verification Log Example

Log output recording authentication and push operations on a successfully executed pipeline node.

$ docker version
Client:
 Version: 29.1.4
 API version: 1.47
 Go version: go1.22.8
 Git commit: 06f9d74
 Built: Wed Nov 12 18:22:10 2026
 OS/Arch: linux/amd64
 Context: default

Server:
 Engine:
 Version: 29.1.4
 API version: 1.47 (minimum version 1.12)
 Go version: go1.22.8
 Git commit: a3f9e2b
 Built: Wed Nov 12 18:21:45 2026
 OS/Arch: linux/amd64
 Experimental: false

$ echo "$HARBOR_PASSWORD" | docker login "$HARBOR_REGISTRY" -u "$HARBOR_USER" --password-stdin
WARNING! Your password will be stored unencrypted in /root/.docker/config.json.
Configure a credential helper to remove this warning. See
https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/login/#credentials-store

Login Succeeded

$ IMAGE_TAG="sha-3b8c1a9e"
$ IMAGE_URI="harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/nginx-app:sha-3b8c1a9e"
$ docker build --pull=false -t "$IMAGE_URI" .
[+] Building 1.2s (6/6) FINISHED
 => [internal] load build definition from Dockerfile
 => => transferring dockerfile: 312B
 => [internal] load metadata for harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/base-nginx:1.25
 => [1/2] FROM harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/base-nginx:1.25
 => [2/2] COPY ./html /usr/share/nginx/html
 => exporting to image
 => => exporting layers
 => => writing image sha256:7f4a21e69b0dc881cb31e5f84918e9c60e42fbe5aa65825cfd9d06b12a8ff93a
 => => naming to harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/nginx-app:sha-3b8c1a9e

$ docker push "$IMAGE_URI"
The push refers to repository [harbor.devstack.co.kr:8443/kubespray/nginx-app]
3f8b091fca1e: Pushed
e6b8b0934c22: Layer already exists
sha-3b8c1a9e: digest: sha256:4d7b29a28e7529841f4812a0f6b3e9491ac9480dcbe82f8a50f3b4dc36f018e6 size: 739

Operational Notes

🛠️ GitLab Runner Tag Management: Ensure Runners in isolated environments are always assigned the docker and offline tags to maintain isolation and prevent build requests from being routed to shared Runners with internet connectivity.

⚠️ dotenv Artifact Expiration: Because expire_in: 7 days is configured, if building pipelines that re-reference metadata from historical jobs older than 7 days, consideration must be given to storing data in an external key-value store or implementing a commit-back mechanism to Git.

💡 Quota Management on Harbor: Untagged intermediate layers and old commit SHA images accumulate easily in Kubespray projects. Therefore, tag retention policies (e.g., retaining the last 20 tags or automatic cleanup after a specified period) must be configured on Harbor.

item.title: Procedure for Building a Local RPM Repository for Kubespray in an Air-Gapped Environment
item.description:
When performing automated Kubernetes cluster construction using Kubespray in an air-gapped environment completely isolated from external networks, it is necessary to procure the required packages for bootstrap processing and OS-level initialization in advance. Simply obtaining and bringing in single RPM packages from an internet-connected environment frequently leads to package installation errors during provisioning due to OS minor version mismatches or missing dependency trees.

This article outlines the procedure for fully collecting all required RPM packages using the dependency resolution flags of dnf on an internet-connected staging host, assuming a Rocky Linux 9.7 environment, and building and verifying a local Yum repository on an internal network Web server.

1. Staging Environment Preparation and Dependency Resolution Mechanism

The internet-connected staging host is configured with the same OS distribution and architecture as the target air-gapped nodes. To traverse the package dependency tree and collect all downstream dependencies without omission, the dnf download command is used after installing the dnf-plugins-core plugin.

sudo dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core

# Create payload storage directories
mkdir -p /data/kubespray-rpms/os
mkdir -p /data/kubespray-rpms/docker-ce-stable

Key Option Specifications for the dnf download Command

Specify the following flags for downloading dependencies:

  • --resolve: Automatically analyzes the entire required dependency graph for the specified packages.
  • --alldeps: Forces all RPM files included in the dependency tree to be targeted for download, even if the packages are already installed on the staging host.
dnf download --resolve --alldeps --destdir=<target_directory> <package_name>

2. RPM Package Acquisition Procedure

2.1 Downloading OS Base Packages and Kubernetes Network Dependencies

Collect the basic tools, network control utilities, and Python bindings required for Ansible execution and Kubespray node setup.

sudo dnf download --resolve --alldeps \
 --destdir=/data/kubespray-rpms/os \
 python3 \
 python3-libselinux \
 conntrack-tools \
 socat \
 iproute \
 iproute-tc \
 iptables \
 ipset \
 ipvsadm \
 ethtool \
 chrony \
 rsync \
 tar \
 unzip \
 curl \
 openssl \
 ca-certificates \
 ebtables

*Note: If the ebtables package is not provided or is deprecated in Enterprise Linux 9 series repositories such as Rocky Linux 9, exclude ebtables from the target list before execution.

sudo dnf download --resolve --alldeps \
 --destdir=/data/kubespray-rpms/os \
 python3 python3-libselinux conntrack-tools socat iproute iproute-tc \
 iptables ipset ipvsadm ethtool chrony rsync tar unzip curl openssl ca-certificates

2.2 Acquiring Container Runtime Dependencies (containerd.io)

Because the standard OS repositories do not contain a production-level containerd.io package, register the official Docker CE repository to retrieve it.

# Add the Docker CE Stable repository
sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo

# Download containerd and SELinux policies
sudo dnf download --resolve --alldeps \
 --destdir=/data/kubespray-rpms/docker-ce-stable \
 containerd.io \
 container-selinux

When adopting the container_manager: containerd configuration in Kubespray, the full docker-ce engine set is not required; configuration is possible with only containerd.io and container-selinux.

3. Creating an Archive and Deploying the Local Repository

Check the volume of the acquired packages and bundle them as a compressed archive.

cd /data
tar czf kubespray-rpms-rocky9.7.tgz kubespray-rpms

Transfer the created archive to an internal mirror server (e.g., Nginx) and extract it under the document root.

sudo mkdir -p /usr/share/nginx/html/ROCKY_9.7
sudo tar xzf kubespray-rpms-rocky9.7.tgz -C /usr/share/nginx/html/ROCKY_9.7

After extraction, execute the createrepo_c utility to generate repository metadata (repodata).

sudo createrepo_c /usr/share/nginx/html/ROCKY_9.7/kubespray-rpms/os
sudo createrepo_c /usr/share/nginx/html/ROCKY_9.7/kubespray-rpms/docker-ce-stable

4. Client Node Configuration and Verification

On the target nodes within the air-gapped environment, disable external repository configurations and create /etc/yum.repos.d/kubespray-local.repo to reference the created local repository.

[kubespray-os]
name=Kubespray OS RPMs
baseurl=http://harbor.devstack.co.kr/ROCKY_9.7/kubespray-rpms/os
enabled=1
gpgcheck=0

[kubespray-containerd]
name=Kubespray Containerd RPMs
baseurl=http://harbor.devstack.co.kr/ROCKY_9.7/kubespray-rpms/docker-ce-stable
enabled=1
gpgcheck=0

Troubleshooting

Case 1: createrepo_c Does Not Exist on the Mirror Server

If the createrepo_c command is not installed on the repository server itself within the air-gapped environment, metadata generation cannot be performed, causing dnf makecache to fail.

Remediation Procedure:
On the internet-connected staging host, acquire createrepo_c itself along with its dependencies in advance, and include it in the payload to bring over.

sudo dnf download --resolve --alldeps \
 --destdir=/data/kubespray-rpms/os \
 createrepo_c

Case 2: Repository Index Synchronization Error and Package Not Found Issues

After configuring the local repository, if old cache remains when executing dnf list, errors indicating missing packages will occur. Explicit execution of cache clearing and index rebuilding is required.

Verification Log Example:

$ sudo dnf clean all
15 files removed

$ sudo dnf makecache
Kubespray OS RPMs 3.2 MB/s | 2.1 MB 00:00 
Kubespray Containerd RPMs 1.8 MB/s | 12 kB 00:00 
Metadata cache created successfully.

$ sudo dnf repolist
repo id repo name
kubespray-containerd Kubespray Containerd RPMs
kubespray-os Kubespray OS RPMs

$ dnf list containerd.io conntrack-tools socat
Available Packages
conntrack-tools.x86_64 1.4.7-2.el9 kubespray-os 
containerd.io.x86_64 1.7.25-3.1.el9 kubespray-containerd
socat.x86_64 1.7.4.1-5.el9 kubespray-os

Lessons Learned

  1. Forced Full Dependency Acquisition: Without the --alldeps option, packages already installed on the staging host will be skipped, posing a risk of missing dependencies on the nodes in the air-gapped environment.
  2. Isolated Management of Container Runtime: Version conflicts can be avoided by individually retrieving containerd.io from the Docker CE repository and indexing it separately from standard OS repositories.
  3. Pre-generation of repodata: Creating metadata with createrepo_c on the repository server before making it available to clients is a mandatory requirement for healthy Yum/DNF package distribution.</package_name></target_directory>
